summary: The regex now matches `[[Target|Label]]` and the label is shown as link text. But the PR builds the URL from the label, not the target. `[[Getting Started|read the guide]]` links to `/read_the_guide/` when it should link to `/Getting_Started/`. That breaks the issue's main requirement: same URL as `[[Getting Started]]`, only the visible text changes. A custom `build_url` also receives the label instead of the target. The PR's tests only check the visible text, so they don't catch this.

own_checks.check: [[Getting Started|read the guide]] links to /Getting_Started/ with text 'read the guide'
own_checks.command: python -c "import markdown; print(markdown.markdown('[[Getting Started|read the guide]]', extensions=['wikilinks']))"

own_checks.check: Whitespace around the pipe is ignored and the URL is still built from the target
A custom build_url, base_url, end_url and html_class get the target, not the label
own_checks.command: python -c "... WikiLinkExtension(base_url='/wiki/', end_url='.html', html_class='wl', build_url=lambda l,b,e: 'X:'+l) ..."
own_checks.output_excerpt: read the guide

findings.title: The URL is built from the display label instead of the target page
findings.evidence: `label = (m.group(2) or m.group(1)).strip()` is then passed to `self.config['build_url'](label, base_url, end_url)`. Running markdown.markdown('[[Getting Started|read the guide]]', extensions=['wikilinks']) gives href="/read_the_guide/" but should give "/Getting_Started/". The target (group 1) has to go to build_url, and only a.text should use group 2.

findings.title: The tests never check href, so they miss the wrong URL
findings.evidence:
Both tests only do assertIn('>read the guide', html). They pass even though the href is wrong. They should compare the full output, e.g. '

read the guide

', and also cover base_url/end_url/html_class/build_url with a label.

notes: docs/extensions/wikilinks.md is not updated to describe the new `[[Target|Label]]` syntax. This is worth adding but does not block the PR.
The label character class `[\w0-9_ -]` is narrow: labels with punctuation such as `[[Page|Read this!]]` won't match. This does not block the PR, but consider allowing a wider label set.
